fields.why: Outcomes are measured per group and compared across 3+ race/ethnicity groups and 5 age groups (diagnosis, PrEP, adherence, suppression, stigma medians).
Race/ethnicity and age are the only SPDs compared across 3+ groups; sex and SOGI only define the MSM population.

The nonoverlap rule in the Table 3 note covers only the stigma medians, so the 'higher than White' and 'highest' (18-24) stigma claims are per-group vs referent only; the NHSS diagnosis, NHSS infection-change and NHBS PrEP comparisons have no stated rule and stay side by side, so the mechanical flags on entries 2-4 are false positives. Minor: entry 3 has n_groups 6 but Table 1 shows 5 age groups with diagnosis estimates, and the 'did not differ by race/ethnicity' and 'by age group' NHBS claims got no entry (side by side, which changes no value).

brief_issues: Entry 4 (z-test of 2010 vs 2019 within each race group, headlined as 'decreased among White MSM but not among Black or Hispanic/Latino MSM') sits between rule 6 (a within-level non-SPD test makes no entry by itself) and rule 4 (time trends compared across 3+ SPD groups are groupwise); a rule saying whether a headline contrast of within-group changes counts as side by side would decide it.
